title: Describing Things and Explaining Their Importance
summary: We talked about our valuable and sentimental possessions and listened to three people describing objects that are important to them. We learned to describe what an object is made of, what it looks like, what it has got and what it is used for, and to explain why it matters to us. Then we described a lost object at a Lost Property Office.

grammar.title: have got / has got to describe objects
grammar.explain: We use have got / has got to say what parts or features an object has. With 'it' we say 'it has got', usually shortened to 'it's got'. Don't use 'a' with plural nouns.
grammar.explain_ar: نستخدم have got / has got لنقول ما في الشيء من أجزاء أو مزايا. مع it نقول it has got وتُختصر غالباً إلى it's got، ومع I/you/we/they نقول have got. لا نستخدم a قبل الأسماء الجمع.
form: It has got (It's got) + a / an + singular noun: It's got a handle.
It has got (It's got) + plural noun: It's got brass locks.
I / you / we / they have got (I've got): I've got an old watch.
Question: Has it got a lid? → Yes, it has. / No, it hasn't.

examples.en: It's got a really high resolution camera.
It's made of black leather and it's got brass locks.

examples.note: A yes/no question in the guessing game.

mistakes.right: It's got buttons. / It's got a button.

mistakes.why: Make the question by moving 'has' to the front.

quiz.why: Questions with 'have got' start with Has/Have.

quiz.q: I ___ an old watch from my grandfather.

grammar.title: Describing an object: made of, adjectives, used for
grammar.explain: To describe an object, we say what material it is made of, what it looks like and what it is used for. After 'used for' we use the -ing form of the verb.
grammar.explain_ar: لوصف شيء ما نذكر المادة المصنوع منها باستخدام made of، ثم شكله وحجمه وحالته بالصفات، ثم الغرض منه باستخدام used for. بعد used for نستخدم الفعل بصيغة ‎-ing (مثل used for cutting)، ويمكن أيضاً أن نقول used to + المصدر.
form: It's made of + material: It's made of leather / wood / metal / plastic / glass.
It's + adjective (shape, size, quality): It's rectangular / tiny / brand new / reliable.
It's used for + verb-ing: It's used for writing / carrying things / cooking.
It's used to + base verb: It's used to carry things.

examples.en: It's made of metal and plastic. It's got two connected parts and it's used for cutting something.
examples.note: A pair of scissors (from the handout).
Shape and size of David's briefcase.

examples.en: Well, it's white and very slim.
examples.note: Colour and shape of Jo's phone.

mistakes.right: It's rectangular. / It's a rectangular box.
mistakes.why: Don't use 'a' before an adjective with no noun.

quiz.q: A pair of scissors is used for ___.

quiz.why: Use the adjective alone, or 'a rectangular shape'.

quiz.q: It's made of leather. It's ___ for carrying papers.
